quiz.question: What happens to Chihiro’s parents after they eat the unattended food?
quiz.explanation: Chihiro finds that her parents have been transformed into pigs.
evidence_markers: parents have been transformed into pigs

quiz.question: Who works in the bathhouse boiler room?
quiz.explanation: Kamaji is the bathhouse’s boiler-man, whom Haku tells Chihiro to approach for work.

quiz.question: How does Yubaba keep people under her control?
options: By taking their memories of home
quiz.explanation: Haku explains that Yubaba controls people by taking their names. Remembering her own name is vital for Chihiro.
evidence_markers: Yubaba controls people by taking their names

quiz.question: What is Chihiro’s first bathhouse customer revealed to be?
quiz.explanation: Her first customer is the spirit of a polluted river, which she cleans.
evidence_markers: spirit of a polluted river arrives as Chihiro's first customer

quiz.question: What does No-Face offer the bathhouse workers in exchange for food?
quiz.explanation: No-Face gives the workers gold while demanding food. Chihiro declines his gold.

quiz.question: What has Haku stolen from Zeniba?
quiz.explanation: Zeniba says Haku stole her magic golden seal, which carries a deadly curse.
evidence_markers: Haku has stolen a magic golden seal

quiz.question: How is Zeniba related to Yubaba?
Where does No-Face choose to stay near the end?
quiz.explanation: No-Face stays with Zeniba while Haku flies Chihiro and Boh back.
evidence_markers: No-Face decides to stay with Zeniba

quiz.question: What is Haku’s true identity?
options: The spirit of the Kohaku River
quiz.explanation: Chihiro remembers the Kohaku River and recognizes Haku as its spirit, restoring his memory.
evidence_markers: Haku's true identity as the spirit of the Kohaku River

quiz.question: What answer lets Chihiro pass Yubaba’s final pig test?
options: None of the pigs are her parents
The two smallest pigs are her parents
All the pigs are her parents
The pigs beside Yubaba are her parents
quiz.explanation: Chihiro correctly recognizes that her parents are not among the pigs shown to her.
evidence_markers: none of the pigs are her parents

facts.title: A heroine for the girls at the cabin
facts.text: Miyazaki wanted to make a film for five young family friends who spent summers at his mountain cabin.
evidence_markers: five girls who were friends of the family

facts.title: A small door sparked a whole world
facts.text: A bathhouse in Miyazaki’s hometown had a small door beside a bathtub. His curiosity about what lay behind it inspired stories that fed the film’s bathhouse setting.
evidence_markers: small door next to one of the bathtubs

facts.title: Architecture gathered from a museum
facts.text: Miyazaki visited Tokyo’s Edo-Tokyo Open Air Architectural Museum during production. Some spirit-world buildings drew on the museum’s Meiji-era Pseudo-Western architecture.

facts.title: A full orchestra for the spirit world
facts.text: Joe Hisaishi composed and conducted the score, which was performed by the New Japan Philharmonic.

facts.title: A closing song found a new home
facts.text: Always With Me was originally intended for another Miyazaki film, Rin the Chimney Painter, which was never released. It became Spirited Away’s closing song.
